request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet where someone already has the same name or alias now merges them into that person instead of refusing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What happens on a merge-transfer:**
- The arriving person's claims go to the matching person, listed after their existing claims. They get the other sheet's next claim numbers and lose any figure a statement had bound.
- The arriving person's name and aliases are added to the matching person's aliases, name first.
- Their grades and contact are dropped, so a contact that's already on the other sheet no longer blocks this kind of transfer.
- The other sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet id>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its rollup lines.
- The sheet they leave writes the same lines as before.

**Still refused:**
- If the matching person on the other sheet is retired, as a merge would refuse.
- If the arriving name and aliases match more than one person there. The request didn't cover this, so I chose to refuse rather than guess who to merge into.
- If nobody on the other sheet matches, the old checks apply unchanged, including the name/alias checks across a sheet's tree and the contact check.

**One thing that differs from an ordinary merge:** I didn't create the arriving person and then reuse the existing merge code. The database allows only one person per sheet with a given name, ignoring case, so creating them first would fail on the match itself. Instead, the claims move straight to the matching person and the aliases are added to them. The rest of what a merge carries over (patrons, pool memberships, holds, watches) doesn't apply, because a transfer drops those anyway.

The changes are in `person/TransferPerson.java` and a small new `joinAliases` method in `person/PersonRepository.java`. The front end needed no changes.
